job.title: Head of Finance
job.description:
About the business
Our client is a well-established, founder-led healthcare group running a portfolio of brands across multiple sites. The portfolio covers premium services, a high-volume growth brand and vertically integrated businesses that support the wider group.

The growth brand runs on the group's own tech-enabled operating platform. It's built to scale, and the founders have serious national expansion plans. The business is profitable, well capitalised and investing heavily in technology and growth.

The group has grown to a point where it needs a true finance leader: someone who can partner with the founders, bring commercial rigour to big decisions and build a finance function ready for the next stage.

The opportunity
This is not a bookkeeping role. The core accounting engine is in place, with a cloud accounting platform, an established payroll system and long-standing external accountants supporting statutory and tax work.

The business now needs someone who understands that engine, makes sure it runs reliably and automatically, and spends their time where it matters most: planning, analysis, insight and growth.

Reporting directly to the co-founders, you'll be the senior finance voice in the business. You'll contribute to leadership-team decisions well beyond finance and help shape the strategy of a business with significant ambitions.

Key responsibilities

Strategic and commercial finance

  • Act as a trusted business partner to the founders and leadership team, turning numbers into clear, actionable insight.
  • Lead financial planning, budgeting and forecasting across the group and its brands.
  • Build the commercial models behind growth decisions, including new site economics, pricing for the platform and partner arrangements, and return on investment.
  • Benchmark and advise on practice-level performance and spend, including marketing, staffing and operating costs, to help each site run at its best.
  • Support funding, investment and expansion planning as the business scales nationally.

Leadership and the finance function

  • Lead, develop and get the best from a small team of in-house and offshore finance staff.
  • Review the structure and capability of the team and shape it for the future.
  • Set clear standards, processes and controls across the function.
  • Bring presence and credibility: hold your own with founders and senior leaders, and be seen as a peer at the leadership table.

Systems, automation and reporting

  • Drive automation across the finance function, working with the in-house tech team as the platform automates more processes, including clinician payments.
  • Get the most out of the cloud accounting and payroll platforms and integrate them with practice management and CRM systems.
  • Deliver timely, accurate and insightful group-level management reporting, consolidated across the brands and sites.
  • Work closely with site managers and the leadership team to make sure financial data flowing from the clinics is accurate and useful.

Compliance and governance

  • Manage the relationship with the external accountants on statutory, tax and audit work.
  • Oversee payroll tax, superannuation and clinician contractor arrangements, which are complex and high-priority in the healthcare sector.
  • Over time, assess which external work could come in-house as the function matures.

About you

  • CA or CPA qualified, with a strong record in strategic, commercial or management accounting.
  • Experience as Head of Finance, Financial Controller or CFO in a growing, multi-site or founder-led business.
  • Healthcare, dental, medical or allied health experience is highly regarded but not essential.
  • A forward thinker who builds scalable systems and automation rather than doing things by hand.
  • Strong commercial instincts, comfortable advising on pricing, unit economics and investment decisions.
  • A confident, credible communicator who can influence founders and senior leaders.
  • A hands-on leader who can develop a small team and lift its performance.
  • Ambitious and genuinely invested in growing your career alongside a scaling business.

Key Benefits

  • A true leadership role with direct access to the founders and real influence on strategy.
  • The chance to shape and build the finance function of a business with big national ambitions.
  • A dynamic, entrepreneurial and values-driven culture.
  • A competitive salary package that reflects the seniority of the role.
  • A Sydney CBD office, with flexibility available once you're established in the business.

job.title: Head of Production & Supply
job.description:
The Opportunity

This is a rare chance to step into the most senior operational leadership role at one of Australia's most respected fresh produce and food manufacturing businesses. Working with the CEO at the helm and a clear mandate for performance and growth, this is the right moment to join and the right role to make your mark.

Reporting directly to the Group CEO, you'll have full end-to-end accountability for a fast-paced, 7-day production facility in North Western Sydney. This is a genuine GM role: you own the P&L, you lead the team, and you drive the results.

About the Business

An Australian family-owned agribusiness with over 50 years of operation. Vertically integrated across production, wholesale distribution, and supplies, this business supplies premium produce to major supermarket chains, leading restaurant groups, and specialist grocers nationally.

This is not a large corporate. It's a lean, high-performing business where every leader's impact is highly visible and where the right person will have genuine influence over the direction of the operation.

About the Role

As the Head of Production & Supply, you'll lead a team of approximately 50 people across production, packaging, warehousing, maintenance, quality, and safety. Your 7 direct reports span Quality & Food Safety, Production Supervisors, Maintenance, Projects, and Warehousing & Logistics.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead day-to-day operations of the production facility, output, quality, and service levels
  • Own the site P&L and operational cost base, including labour, materials, packaging, and utilities
  • Drive a continuous improvement culture using Lean/Six Sigma methodologies to reduce waste and lift throughput
  • Manage all cold chain, warehousing, and dispatch operations to full food safety compliance
  • Own the end-to-end supply chain, including direct relationships with produce growers and exotic variety suppliers
  • Maintain HACCP, SQF, and all food safety and WHS compliance obligations
  • Partner with the CEO and senior leadership team on performance reporting, cost initiatives, and growth strategy
  • Build a high-performance, safety-first culture across a diverse workforce


Beyond the day-to-day, the incoming Head of Production & Supply is expected to deliver five priority outcomes: renegotiate supplier contracts and drive cost out quickly; implement ERP across the pack house; build the capex case for a new slicing line; rebuild and upskill the production, maintenance, and distribution team; and set a compelling cultural direction for the site.

About You

You're an experienced operational leader from food manufacturing, fresh produce, FMCG, or a similarly fast-paced perishable goods environment. You've run a production site end-to-end and you've owned the numbers, not just the floor.

You'll bring:

  • Significant experience in a senior operational or site leadership role (GM, Site Manager, Operations Manager, or equivalent)
  • Proven track record of P&L accountability and cost performance in a manufacturing or production environment
  • Deep knowledge of lean manufacturing, CI methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent), and structured problem-solving
  • Experience in supply chain management, cold chain logistics, and/or supplier relationship management
  • Exceptional people leadership across a large, diverse workforce
  • The drive to be present, hands-on, and genuinely invested in the operation


Why This Role

  • Report directly to the CEO, genuine influence from day one
  • Full P&L ownership and end-to-end operational accountability
  • Be part of a small, high-impact executive team at a genuine business inflection point
  • Competitive base salary + superannuation + performance incentive

job.title: Financial Controller - ANZ
job.description:
About the business

Our client is an ASX-listed manufacturer and distributor that places a strong emphasis on passion, collaboration, and innovation. This is a hands-on role, working closely with senior management and playing a critical role in financial reporting, while serving as a key business partner to the Group Executive. You’ll be joining a close-knit, high-performing team that takes ownership, challenges the status quo, and brings energy and enthusiasm to everything they do. They operate across Australia and New Zealand, with its own offshore manufacturing.

About the role

Reporting to the Group Controller ANZ, you'll lead financial control and finance operations across Australia and New Zealand. This is a hands-on leadership role in an inventory-intensive business. You'll own the close, consolidation, statutory reporting, treasury and controls, and you'll be a trusted finance partner to the MD, the country GMs and the commercial and operational leaders.

Key responsibilities:

Financial operations and reporting

  • Own the monthly, half-year and year-end close across all AU and NZ entities, targeting working day 5.
  • Oversee AP, AR, payroll, the general ledger and inventory accounting, and own the balance sheet reconciliation framework.
  • Prepare consolidated AU and NZ management accounts, with insight by country, channel, customer and product category.
  • Lead or support budgeting, forecasting and scenario modelling.

Consolidation and statutory

  • Prepare the AU and NZ group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations and unrealised profit.
  • Coordinate statutory accounts for all AU and NZ entities.

Treasury, working capital and inventory

  • Manage cash forecasting, banking relationships, facilities and covenant reporting.
  • Monitor FX exposures and support hedging decisions.
  • Drive working capital improvements across debtors, creditors and stock.
  • Oversee inventory valuation, landed costs, freight, rebates, stocktakes and provisioning.
  • Support product costing and margin analysis for manufactured and imported product.

Tax, audit and controls

  • Ensure BAS, GST, FBT, payroll tax and NZ tax compliance.
  • Coordinate income tax and transfer pricing with Group Finance and advisers.
  • Lead the ANZ external audit.
  • Maintain a strong control environment across order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, inventory, treasury and record-to-report.

Systems and process improvement

  • Play a lead role in the NetSuite rollout for ANZ, from process design and data through to testing and adoption.
  • Simplify and standardise processes, and reduce manual effort.

Leadership and partnering

  • Lead, coach and develop the AU and NZ finance team.
  • Partner with Sales, Operations, Supply Chain and Warehouse leaders on margin, pricing, inventory and cost performance.

About you

  • CA or CPA qualified, with an audit background.
  • At least 5 years as a Financial Controller or senior finance manager across Australia and New Zealand, ideally in a business turning over $40-100 million.
  • A manufacturing background, with hands-on inventory accounting, standard costing, stocktakes and provisioning.
  • Distribution and retail experience, ideally across wholesale, retail and online channels.
  • A solid understanding of supply chain, including procurement, production planning, landed costs, warehousing and distribution.
  • NetSuite experience, ideally including an implementation or migration.
  • Strong technical accounting, consolidation, audit, tax and treasury capability.
  • A track record of leading finance teams and partnering with senior non-finance stakeholders.

Highly regarded:

  • Offshore manufacturing or imported product exposure, including FX.
  • Experience in a multi-entity, cross-border group with intercompany and transfer pricing.
  • A listed or private equity-owned environment.
  • A retail apparel or textitle background.

What's on offer

  • Attractive Salary Package.
  • One day a week working from home after the first 3 months, which are fully office-based.
  • Free onsite parking.
  • A visible role in a growing international group, with close exposure to group finance leadership.
  • The chance to shape ANZ finance processes and systems through a major ERP transition.

job.title: Assistant Accountant
job.description:
A rare opportunity to make your mark

Most assistant accountant roles ask you to slot into a process someone else built years ago. This one is different.

Our client is a long-established Melbourne manufacturer with a proud history, loyal long-term customers and around 100 dedicated staff. In October 2026 it began a new chapter as a standalone business under new ownership. With new owners behind it and a clear vision for growth, the business is now bringing its finance function fully in-house for the first time.

That's where you come in. As the business's first in-house assistant accountant, you'll take ownership of the processes that keep money flowing in and out of a business. You'll build the way things are done, and you'll be recognised for it.

Why this role stands out

  • Real ownership from day one. You won't be one person in a large shared-services queue. You'll own AP and AR end-to-end, and your work will be visible to the leadership team and the business's owners.
  • A genuine pathway to permanent. The 6-month fixed term gives both sides the chance to get to know each other. The business is actively shaping its long-term finance structure, and the right person will have every opportunity to make the role their own permanently.
  • Room to grow beyond transactions. Alongside the core AP/AR work, you'll prepare cash flow reporting and forecasting for senior leadership. That experience is ideal for anyone working towards their CPA and a broader finance career. As the business evolves, so can the role.
  • Rewarded for seeing it through. On top of a competitive salary, you'll receive a completion bonus when you finish the 6-month term.
  • Flexibility that works. Hybrid working is supported, with a minimum of 2 days a week on site in Thomastown, where you'll be close to the operation and the team.
  • A stable, relationship-driven business. Around 80% of customers are on contract and most of the rest are repeat clients. You'll be working with people the business knows well, not chasing difficult debt.

What you'll be doing

Accounts Payable

  • Processing around 3,000 supplier invoices a year end-to-end in SAP, including receipting, coding, matching, approvals and payment runs
  • Resolving supplier queries and keeping supplier accounts accurate and up to date
  • Reconciling supplier statements

Accounts Receivable

  • Allocating customer receipts and reconciling against bank statements
  • Monitoring the debtors ledger and keeping customers to their trading terms
  • Following up overdue accounts by email and phone, and working with the sales team on pricing or quality queries
  • Building strong working relationships with key customers

Cash Flow and Reporting

  • Completing daily bank reconciliations
  • Preparing daily and weekly cash position reporting
  • Building short-term cash flow forecasts for the local leadership team and the business's owners

Process and Documentation

  • Learning existing processes during a structured handover from the previous finance provider
  • Documenting procedures clearly so the business has a reliable, long-term finance playbook
  • Recommending and implementing improvements as the function settles in

About you

You're an assistant accountant or experienced AP/AR professional who enjoys ownership and takes pride in getting the details right. You'll ideally bring:

  • 4+ years' experience in accounts payable, accounts receivable or an assistant accountant role
  • SAP experience (highly regarded)
  • A degree in accounting or finance, or current study towards one; CPA/CA candidates are strongly encouraged to apply
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and confidence speaking with customers and suppliers on the phone
  • Strong organisational skills and accuracy, including with manual processing
  • An instinct for structure: you like documenting processes and leaving things better than you found them
  • A proactive, self-starting attitude, and you're comfortable working closely with a manager who is sometimes remote
  • Availability to start in late October or early November

Manufacturing experience is a bonus but not essential. Attitude, accuracy and communication matter most.

What's on offer

  • Attractive base salary plus superannuation, depending on experience
  • A completion bonus paid on successfully finishing the 6-month term
  • A genuine opportunity to convert to a permanent role
  • Hybrid working, with a minimum of 2 days a week on site in Thomastown
  • Direct exposure to senior leadership and the business's owners
  • Practical, broad finance experience to support your CPA journey and career growth
  • A supportive, close-knit team in a business entering an exciting new phase
  • A quick, streamlined interview process

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
About the Company

A high-growth, privately backed Australian business with a strong national footprint and an ambitious trajectory. The company designs, manufactures, and distributes specialised solutions across Australia and operates with the pace and accountability of a scale-up, underpinned by serious financial backing and a seasoned executive leadership team.

About the Role

This is not your typical EA role and we are not looking for a typical EA. An opportunity has opened up for an experienced, operationally sharp Executive Assistant to join a high-growth Australian business in a role that sits right at the centre of everything.

You will report directly to the CEO and work closely with the broader leadership team, but your remit goes well beyond the traditional executive support function. This is a broad, high-trust position where you will have genuine influence over how the business operates and where no two weeks will look the same.

One day you are preparing materials for a leadership meeting and coordinating interstate travel. The next you are onboarding a new team member, managing the company's social media presence, or owning the logistics for a national trade exhibition. You will be the person the business leans on to keep things moving, the one who brings structure where there is ambiguity and calm where there is pressure.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Executive support to the CEO and senior leaders including calendar management, communications, board deliverables, meeting preparation, and follow-up
  • Sending out employment contracts and managing the full onboarding process for new starters
  • Coordinating domestic and international travel for executives, customers, and key stakeholders
  • End-to-end ownership and delivery of major events including national exhibitions and conferences
  • Day-to-day office management covering facilities, suppliers, WHS compliance, and general operations
  • Managing and maintaining the company's social media channels and supporting broader marketing and brand activities
  • HR administration across the employee lifecycle including performance coordination, records management, and offboarding

About You

You have done something like this before, maybe not under this exact title, but you know what it means to be the operational engine of a small, fast-moving business. You are the person who sees what needs to happen before anyone asks, who builds the process when there is not one, and who holds things together when everyone else is focused on the bigger picture.

You are highly organised without being rigid. Professionally polished without being precious. You can walk out of a senior leadership meeting, deal with a supplier, post something on Instagram, and sort out the catering for tomorrow's client visit, all before lunch, and none of it will faze you. You take genuine pride in doing things properly, and you understand that the small stuff is never really small.

You are the kind of person who does not think twice about the milk run, the courier, or the office supply order, because you understand that keeping a business running well means owning all of it, not just the parts that look impressive on a CV.

You thrive in environments where you are trusted to get on with it. Where the leadership team knows you are across it so they do not have to be. Where your contribution is visible not because you push for recognition, but because the business simply runs better when you are in it.

You will bring:

  • Proven experience in a broad EA, office management, or executive operations role, you have been the go-to person and you know what that means in practice
  • Confidence and quiet authority with senior executives and leadership teams — you manage upwards as naturally as you manage everything else
  • Exceptional organisational skills and the ability to hold multiple priorities simultaneously without anything slipping through the cracks
  • Strong written and verbal communication with a professional, considered style that adapts effortlessly to the audience, whether that is a board paper or an Instagram caption
  • Hands-on experience with HR platforms, contract management and DocuSign, corporate travel systems, and social media management
  • A proactive, solutions-first mindset, you do not wait to be told, you figure it out and you fix it
  • The maturity and discretion to handle sensitive information, confidential matters, and high-stakes situations with absolute integrity

Key Benefits

  • Attractive salary package plus performance bonus
  • Four days per week in the office with one flexible WFH day
  • A high-impact, central role working directly alongside an experienced and engaged executive team
  • Broad exposure across operations, HR, events, and commercial activity
  • A collaborative, high-performing culture that genuinely values contribution
  • The opportunity to grow with a business that is on a strong and sustained upward trajectory
